title: Finite labeled embedded blowup towers and synchronized comparison data
statement: An embedded pair over $\mathbf Q$ consists of a reduced scheme $X$ closed immersed in a smooth separated finite-type scheme $P$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For a totally ordered set $L$, a finite labeled embedded resolution tower is a finite set of active labels and diagrams of ambient schemes and embedded strict transforms indexed contravariantly by lower cuts of $L$. The empty cut is the given pair, the full cut has regular strict transform [def-weil-regular-scheme], and any interval containing no active label is an isomorphism. At each label $l$, the center is a quasi-coherent ideal on the ambient scheme before $l$, together with its closed immersion into the strict transform. At an active label the center is nonempty, regular and nowhere dense in the strict transform (its range has empty interior), and has coherent ideal on both schemes [pqf-def-coherent]; the next ambient scheme and strict transform are respectively the ordinary blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] and the scheme-theoretic strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform], with their structure maps. At every absent label the center is the unit ideal, hence the stage is an identity up to the specified diagram isomorphisms. Once a strict transform is regular no active labels remain; empty and regular inputs have no active labels. A smooth comparison is a pair of natural transformations of these diagrams lifting a cartesian smooth ambient map, cartesian over the initial schemes at every cut and identifying each center ideal with its pullback; it retains exactly the labels whose pulled-back centers are nonempty. An intrinsic comparison along an isomorphism of initial reduced schemes is a natural isomorphism of the strict-transform diagrams with that initial component, preserving labels and intrinsic center ideals. A synchronized embedded resolution assignment consists of such a tower for every embedded pair (including finite disjoint unions), smooth comparisons satisfying identity and composition, and intrinsic comparisons satisfying identity and the cocycle for three inputs. These are data and conditions, not an assertion that an assignment exists.

source.place: Expose VIII 2.3.1, 2.3.4, 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.91--94; labeled data implementing the synchronization convention. Bierstone--Milman--Temkin, Q-universal desingularization, arXiv:0905.3580, Theorem 6.1 and Addendum, section 6.3 (online source read).
